title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This page continues the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'. Π̂_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of U_{0,3} = P^1 − {0,1,∞}, with loop generators l_0, l_1, l_∞ satisfying l_0 l_1 l_∞ = 1. M^{!~}_{0,3} is the group of 'automorphismes à lacets' of Π̂_{0,3} that commute exteriorly with the S_3-symmetries. It is an extension of an outer group N^{!~}_{0,3} (a GT/Galois-type group) by the inner automorphisms Π̂_{0,3}. M^{~}_{0,3} is the analogous extension by Ŝ^+_{0,3}. By the next page Ŝ^+_{0,3} is generated by σ_∞ (order 2) and ρ (order 3), with φ̂: Π̂_{0,3} → Ŝ^+_{0,3}. So Ŝ^+_{0,3} is in effect the profinite completion of PSL_2(Z) ≅ Z/2 * Z/3, which contains Π̂_{0,3} = Γ(2)/±1 with index 6.

Previous page. M^{!~}[0] is the subgroup of u preserving the inertia subgroup L_0 = <l_0>^ up to conjugation; it acts on L_0 and its normalizer through a matrix (μ M; 0 1). One shows M ≡ 0 mod 2. Composing with the inner automorphism by l_0^{M/2} then kills M. So M^{!~}(0), the set of u with u(l_0) = l_0^μ exactly (the 'normalized' u), is a section subgroup of each of the three extensions.

This page.
(1) Every u is uniquely written u = f^{-1} u_ξ with u_ξ normalized. This is the semidirect product decomposition (180): M^{!~}_{0,3} ≅ M^{!~}(0) ⋉ Π̂_{0,3}. Likewise (181): M^{~}_{0,3} ≅ M^{!~}(0) ⋉ Ŝ^+_{0,3}.
(2) Remark. These 'canonical' splittings should be examined in relation with the choice of a uniformizer at 0 on P^1_Q, the smooth compactification of U_{0,3,Q}. In modern terms, this is a tangential base point at 0. Over Q the arithmetic section of π_1 attached to a 'point at infinity' depends on the uniformizer t, up to Kummer twists when t is rescaled by c ∈ Q^*. The question is which uniformizer realizes the group-theoretically canonical section.
(3) The same construction, done in the normalizers of L_1 and L_∞, gives section subgroups M^{!~}(q) for q ∈ {0,1,∞}, see (182). These are permuted by the order-3 symmetry ρ: ρ(M(q)) = M(ρ(q)), see (183). Hence all three come from any one of them via ρ and ρ^2.

Purpose. To fix normal forms (u = f^{-1}u_ξ with f normalized) for solutions of the loop equation, before studying exterior commutation with φ̂ in §47 on the next page.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. Two points are asserted rather than proved on this page. First, M^{!~}(0) ∩ Π̂_{0,3} is trivial; this follows because the normalizer of L_0 in the free profinite group is L_0 itself, and an inner l_0^n has M = 2n, which is 0 only for n = 0. Second, (181) requires M^{!~}(0) ∩ Ŝ^+_{0,3} = 1 inside M^{~}. Both are plausible given the previous page's analysis.

ideas.what: Splitting the extension 'automorphisms → outer automorphisms' of Π̂_{0,3} by normalizing u(l_0) = l_0^μ (no conjugating factor). This is the semidirect decomposition M^{!~} ≅ M(0) ⋉ Π̂_{0,3}.
ideas.modern_name: Normalized lifts of GT / Galois actions on F̂_2 (the standard normal form σ(x) = x^{χ(σ)}, σ(y) = f^{-1} y^{χ(σ)} f) giving Aut-level splitting
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1985–91), Deligne (1989); Belyi–Ihara normal form
ideas.where_published: Possibly sketched in La Longue Marche (1981); not in the Esquisse in this form

ideas.what: The same splitting with the bigger group Ŝ^+_{0,3} (profinite PSL_2(Z)) in place of Π̂_{0,3}.
ideas.modern_name: Section of the outer action on the profinite modular group / S_3-equivariant version of GT
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps (GT acting on Â_1-type groups)

ideas.what: Relating the canonical group-theoretic section to the choice of a uniformizer at the cusp 0 of P^1_Q. The section depends on the 'point at infinity' plus a uniformizer, i.e. a tangential base point.
ideas.modern_name: Tangential base points (01→ etc.) and their dependence on the tangent vector via Kummer cocycles
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne 1989 ('Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points'); Ihara; Nakamura
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck discusses 'points à l'infini'/base points in La Longue Marche and the Esquisse; exact formulation unsure

ideas.what: Three section subgroups M(0), M(1), M(∞), one per cusp, permuted by the order-3 symmetry ρ.
ideas.modern_name: Changes of tangential base point among 01→, 10→, ∞-points under the S_3 symmetries of P^1 − {0,1,∞}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne, Ihara, Drinfeld (the cocycle relations of GT encode these path changes)

missed.claim: Grothendieck flags as a task to relate the purely group-theoretic 'canonical' splitting (normalization B = 0) to the choice of a uniformizer at 0. This anticipates the tangential-base-point formalism, but the question is not carried out here. It was later effectively answered by Deligne and Ihara (the normalized splitting corresponds to the tangential base point 01→ with uniformizer z).
missed.quote: Il faudrait à l'occasion examiner de plus près ces scindages canoniques en relation avec le choix d'une uniformisante en 0 de P^1_Q
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly historical. It documents that Grothendieck explicitly linked normalized loop-automorphisms to uniformizers at cusps, i.e. tangential base points, independently of and probably before Deligne 1989.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine normalization and semidirect decomposition. The remark linking the canonical splitting to the choice of a uniformizer is a nice historical anticipation of tangential base points, but that theory is well established and credited (Deligne, Ihara).
transcription_corrections: Rmq line: likely 'Il faudrait à l'occasion examiner de plus près ces scindages canoniques en relation avec le choix d'une uniformisante en 0 de P^1_Q = \hat{U}_{0,3,Q}' rather than 'l'occasion [?] indiquer [?] une autre [?]'.
'la même question se pose pour les deux autres "points à l'infini" 1, ∞' (with 'aux deux autres' an insertion).
'dans la manière du L_0' should read 'dans le normalisateur de L_0'.
Last line: 'se déduisent de l'un quelconque d'entre eux, au moyen des automorphismes ρ, ρ^2' (not 'du 1er au quelconques ... ou au moyen').
